subject.title: Write tool lacks append mode — isolated cron sessions destroy shared files

question: Should OpenClaw expose append as an optional `write.append` parameter, a separate append tool, or a narrower memory/cron-owned primitive for ordinary agent writes?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but changing the model-facing write contract affects public tool semantics, provider schemas, sandbox behavior, and future compatibility.

options.title: Approve optional write append
options.body: Proceed with a backwards-compatible `append: true` parameter if PR review confirms workspace/sandbox guards, mutation queueing, and tool-schema projection remain safe.

options.title: Prefer separate append tool
options.body: Ask the implementation PR to expose append as a distinct model-facing tool so destructive overwrite and append semantics cannot be confused in one schema.

options.title: Keep append scoped
options.body: Limit append behavior to memory/cron-owned flows and leave ordinary `write` overwrite-only, accepting that general agent append remains unsolved.

recommendation.title: Approve optional write append
recommendation.body: Proceed with a backwards-compatible `append: true` parameter if PR review confirms workspace/sandbox guards, mutation queueing, and tool-schema projection remain safe.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current internalized agent-runtime tool surface and are the best available owner for a public tool-contract direction call.
